scene: The plain round target board with five rings hangs on the plain wall, and one plain dart is stuck with its tip in the centre ring, the shaft sticking out straight toward the viewer. The rest of the board and the wall around it are bare.
must: the dart's tip in the centre of the rings.
avoid: a dart in the wall beside the board (mis); a dart in the outer ring (bijna); a dart in the air with no target (not the card); a person throwing a dart (not the frame).
contrast: Pair with mis. The only difference is where the dart ends: in the centre ring here, in the bare wall beside the board there.
alt: Een pijl steekt in het midden van een ronde schijf met cirkels.

scene: The plain round target board with five rings hangs on the plain wall, bare in every ring, and one plain dart is stuck in the wall a hand's width to the right of the board with its tip in the wall, the shaft pointing toward the viewer.
must: a dart in the bare wall beside the board.
avoid: a dart in the centre ring (raak); a dart in the outer ring of the board (bijna); a dart falling on the floor (not the card); a board with no dart at all (not the card).
contrast: Pair with raak. The only difference is where the dart ends: in the bare wall beside the board here, in the centre ring there.
example_nl: Je schot is mis, probeer het nog eens.
example_en: Your shot is off target, try again.
alt: Een pijl steekt in de muur naast een ronde schijf met cirkels die leeg is.

scene: One child stands side-on on the ground line with arms stretched straight up and head tilted back, hands just opened after a throw. A plain round ball hangs high above the hands, three short strokes below it marking its upward path, and the plain wall behind is bare.
must: the ball high above the hands with strokes beneath it and the face tilted up.
avoid: a ball dropping toward the hands with strokes above it (omlaag); a tall tower (hoog); a ball resting on a shelf (boven); a child jumping with the ball in hand (not the card).
contrast: Pair with omlaag. The only difference is the ball's path: strokes below it as it rises away from the hands here, strokes above it as it falls toward the hands there.
example_nl: Kijk omhoog, daar vliegt een vogel.
example_en: Look up, there is a bird flying.
alt: Een kind met de armen gestrekt kijkt naar een bal ver boven zijn handen met drie streepjes eronder.

scene: One child stands side-on on the ground line with arms held low and open and head still tilted back. A plain round ball hangs a little above the hands, three short strokes above it marking its downward path, and the plain wall behind is bare.
must: the ball just above the open hands with strokes above it.
avoid: a ball rising away from the hands with strokes below (omhoog); a ball already on the ground (not the card); a low table (laag); a child bending to pick up a ball (not the card).
contrast: Pair with omhoog. The only difference is the ball's path: strokes above it as it falls toward the hands here, strokes below it as it rises away from the hands there.
example_nl: De lift gaat omlaag naar de kelder.
example_en: The lift is going down to the cellar.
alt: Een kind houdt zijn open handen bij zijn knieën en kijkt naar een bal net boven zijn handen, met drie streepjes erboven.

scene: The plain small car, seen from the side with its front facing right, stands between the two plain posts on the ground line. A short trail of tyre tracks runs on the ground behind the car, from the boot back toward the left post, and the ground ahead of the bonnet is clean.
must: tyre tracks behind the boot and clean ground ahead of the bonnet.
avoid: tracks ahead of the bonnet (achteruit); a car with speed lines (snel); a car turning into a side road (linksaf); a parked car with no tracks (not the card).
contrast: Pair with achteruit. The only difference is the tyre tracks: behind the boot here, ahead of the bonnet there.
alt: Een kleine auto staat tussen twee paaltjes; bij de kofferbak liggen bandensporen, bij de motorkap is de grond schoon.

scene: The plain small car, seen from the side with its front facing right, stands between the two plain posts on the ground line. A short trail of tyre tracks runs on the ground ahead of the car, from the bonnet on toward the right post, and the ground behind the boot is clean.
must: tyre tracks ahead of the bonnet and clean ground behind the boot.
avoid: tracks behind the boot (vooruit); a car with speed lines (snel); a car parked against a wall (not the card); a car being towed (not the card).
contrast: Pair with vooruit. The only difference is the tyre tracks: ahead of the bonnet here, behind the boot there.
example_nl: Hij rijdt de auto achteruit de garage in.
example_en: He reverses the car into the garage.
alt: Een kleine auto staat tussen twee paaltjes; bij de motorkap liggen bandensporen, bij de kofferbak is de grond schoon.

scene: The plain three-way junction in a high three-quarter view from behind the adult, who stands at its foot; a small house stands beside the left branch. A dotted line runs from the adult's feet straight up the middle path to the top edge, while the left and right branches carry no line.
must: a dotted line running straight up the middle branch.
avoid: a dotted line turning into the left branch (linksaf); a dotted line turning into the right branch (rechtsaf); a dotted line that loops back (not the card); a long straight road with no junction (lang).
contrast: Pair with linksaf and rechtsaf. The only difference is the branch with the dotted line: the middle one here, the left one in linksaf, the right one in rechtsaf.
example_nl: Loop rechtdoor tot het einde van de straat.
example_en: Walk straight on to the end of the street.
alt: Een man met zijn rug naar ons staat bij een splitsing; een stippellijn loopt over het middelste pad naar de verte.

scene: The plain three-way junction in a high three-quarter view from behind the adult, who stands at its foot; a small house stands beside the left branch. A dotted line runs from the adult's feet up and bends into the branch on the left side of the picture, ending near its end; the middle and right branches carry no line.
must: a dotted line bending into the left branch.
avoid: a dotted line going straight up the middle (rechtdoor); a dotted line bending into the right branch (rechtsaf); a person turning around to go back (not the card); a U-turn loop (not the card).
contrast: Pair with rechtdoor and rechtsaf. The only difference is the branch with the dotted line: the left one here, the middle one in rechtdoor, the right one in rechtsaf.
example_nl: Bij het stoplicht gaat u linksaf.
example_en: At the traffic light you turn left.
alt: Een man met zijn rug naar ons staat bij een splitsing; een stippellijn buigt naar het pad met het huis.

scene: The plain three-way junction in a high three-quarter view from behind the adult, who stands at its foot; a small house stands beside the left branch. A dotted line runs from the adult's feet up and bends into the branch on the right side of the picture, ending near its end; the middle and left branches carry no line.
must: a dotted line bending into the right branch.
avoid: a dotted line going straight up the middle (rechtdoor); a dotted line bending into the left branch (linksaf); a person turning around to go back (not the card); a U-turn loop (not the card).
contrast: Pair with rechtdoor and linksaf. The only difference is the branch with the dotted line: the right one here, the middle one in rechtdoor, the left one in linksaf.
example_nl: Na de brug gaat u rechtsaf.
example_en: After the bridge you turn right.
alt: Een man met zijn rug naar ons staat bij een splitsing; een stippellijn buigt naar het pad tegenover het huis.

scene: The six plain wooden blocks are stacked and pushed together into one tight cluster in the middle of the table, every block touching at least one other, the outline of the group compact. The rest of the table and the wall behind are bare.
must: all six blocks in one tight cluster.
avoid: blocks spread out one by one (apart); blocks in a tall tower (hoog); blocks lined up in a row with gaps (not the card); a few blocks dropped on the floor (not the card).
contrast: Pair with apart. The only difference is the arrangement: all six blocks touching in one cluster here, six blocks each alone with wide gaps there.
example_nl: Wij wonen met de hele familie bij elkaar.
example_en: We live together as a whole family.
alt: Zes houten blokken liggen als één groepje midden op een tafel, zonder ruimte ertussen.

scene: The six plain wooden blocks lie spread across the table, each one alone with a wide empty gap to the next, none touching another. The rest of the table and the wall behind are bare.
must: six blocks each alone with wide gaps between them.
avoid: all six blocks in one cluster (bij elkaar); blocks piled in a stack (hoog); a few blocks missing from the table (weinig); blocks hidden in a drawer (not the card).
contrast: Pair with bij-elkaar. The only difference is the arrangement: six blocks each alone with wide gaps here, all six touching in one cluster there.
example_nl: Leg het vlees en de groente apart.
example_en: Put the meat and the vegetables apart.
alt: Zes houten blokken liggen elk op een eigen plek met veel lege tafel ertussen.
